title: Race Window
statement: Implement `solve(order)`. `order` is a list of `check-a`, `check-b`, `store-a`, `store-b`. The key starts absent. A check sees a miss only if no store of that same letter has happened yet... Simplify: return `twice` if both checks appear before either store. Return `once` otherwise. `twice` means both threads decided to load.
constraints: Both checks before any store is the race
A store before the second check collapses it
hints: Find the indexes of the two checks and the first store.
If both checks are before the first store, return twice.
Otherwise return once. If there is no store, both checks still return twice.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: The race window is the gap between seeing a miss and storing the value.

editorial: The race window is the gap between seeing a miss and storing the value. If both threads check inside that gap, the key is loaded twice. A store that happens before the second check closes the window. The interleaving is the input. You do not need threads to classify it.
